summary: Five defects in CardSorting's pointer path, two of which changed the user's data. Closes #21. (1) `pointercancel` called the same endDrag as `pointerup`, so it announced "dropped" and KEPT the move; on touch, pointercancel is the browser taking the gesture away (a scroll takeover, an OS gesture), and the portal saves on settle, so it persisted a move the person abandoned. It now restores the order from before the gesture, calls onOrderChange once more with that order, and announces cancelled. (2) Escape only cancelled a keyboard/click LIFT; during a pointer drag it did nothing. It now cancels a drag the same way, listened for on the document while a drag is live, because a press does not focus a button in every browser (Safari) and the person pressing Escape mid-drag is not thinking about focus. (3) The handle's onClick always toggled lift, and a comment claimed pointerup had already cleared the drag so it would not; the handler never read that state. With the pointer captured on the grip, the click after pointerup lands on it, so every finished drag also lifted the row. A press now becomes a drag only after 4px of travel; a press that moves less is still a click and still lifts (the SC 2.5.7 single-pointer path), and the click that ends a real drag is swallowed. A side effect worth knowing: a plain click no longer announces "dropped" before "lifted" for a drag that never happened. (4) Any button started a drag, including right and middle clicks; only event.button === 0 does now. (5) setPointerCapture throws NotFoundError for a pointer that is no longer active, which broke the handler before the drag began; it and releasePointerCapture are wrapped in try/catch. Each case has a browser test, and all eight new pointer tests fail against the previous component, checked by swapping it back in.

migration.manual: If you added your own restore-on-pointercancel or settle detection around onOrderChange to work around this, remove it: a cancelled gesture now calls onOrderChange with the restored order itself, and doing both restores twice. A drag now needs 4px of pointer travel before rows move.
